message.content:
Yes – you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta’s local authorities.  
In the United States, “local council” usually refers to the city’s governing body (the City Council), but noise complaints are typically handled by the city’s **Police Department** or **Code Enforcement** office.  

Below is a quick guide on how to report a noise issue in Atlanta:

| Step | What to Do | Where / How |
|------|------------|-------------|
| **1. Identify the problem** | Note the source (e.g., a neighbor’s party, construction, loud music), the time it started, and how long it continues. | Keep a brief log or take a short video if you feel it’s necessary. |
| **2. Check the noise ordinance** | Atlanta’s Noise Ordinance (Title 10, Chapter 1, § 10‑1‑1) sets limits on decibel levels and hours of operation. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/CityHall/CityCode/Noise> |
| **3. Contact the Police Department** | For non‑emergencies, call the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line at **404‑656‑4000**. If the situation is urgent (e.g., ongoing disturbance, safety concern), call **911**. | Phone or in‑person visit to the nearest precinct. |
| **4. File an online complaint** | Use the City of Atlanta’s 311 portal to submit a noise complaint. You’ll receive a reference number and an estimated response time. | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| **5. Follow up** | If you don’t hear back within the timeframe indicated (usually 24–48 hrs for non‑emergencies), call the non‑emergency line again or check the status online. | Phone or 311 portal. |
| **6. Keep records** | Save any correspondence, reference numbers, or notes from police visits. | Email, printouts, or a digital folder. |

### Quick Contact Details

| Agency | Phone | Address | Online Portal |
|--------|-------|---------|---------------|
| Atlanta Police Department (Non‑Emergency) | 404‑656‑4000 | 1000 Peachtree St NW, Atlanta, GA 30309 | N/A |
| City of Atlanta 311 | 404‑656‑4000 (same line) | Same as above | <https://www.atlantaga.gov/311> |
| City Hall (for official council matters) | 404‑656‑4000 | 1000 Peachtree St NW, Atlanta, GA 30309 | <https://www.atlantaga.gov> |

### Tips & Best Practices

- **Be polite but firm** when speaking to officers or filling out forms.  
- **Provide specifics**: exact location, time, and description of the noise.  
- **Use the 311 portal** if you prefer a written record; it automatically logs your complaint and assigns a case number.  
- **If the noise is from a commercial establishment**, you can also contact the Atlanta Business Improvement District (BID) or the local zoning office.  
- **Check local bylaws**: Some neighborhoods have homeowners’ association (HOA) rules that supplement city ordinances.  

### Bottom Line

Yes, you can report a noise complaint to the City of Atlanta. The most direct route is through the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line or the city’s 311 online portal. Once filed, the city will investigate and take appropriate action—often involving a warning, citation, or, in extreme cases, a police intervention.
